units.text: INT. GRANDMOTHER'S SEWING ROOM - AFTERNOON
A narrow room at the back of a Calabrian apartment, sun slanting through yellowed lace.
Bolts of fabric lean in corners like tired dancers.
A black Singer sits under a crocheted cloth, a pincushion shaped like a tomato beside it.
ROSALBA GRIECO, 80, tiny, black dress, hair in a white bun, kneels on a cushion pinning a hem.
CARMELINA GRIECO, 50s, her daughter, stands on the fitting stool in a half-finished wedding dress, arms out like a scarecrow.
ISOTTA, 22, the granddaughter, sits cross-legged on the bed, picking at the chenille.
You've lost weight.
units.name: ROSALBA

units.text: I haven't.
units.name: CARMELINA

units.text: The hips are loose.
units.name: ROSALBA

units.text: It's the way you cut it.
units.name: CARMELINA

units.text: I cut it for the bride. Not for you. For Isotta.
units.name: ROSALBA

units.text: It's not my dress, Nonna.
units.name: ISOTTA

units.text: Of course it is. You're the one marrying.
units.name: ROSALBA

units.text: I'm not marrying anyone.
units.name: ISOTTA

units.text: Isotta.
units.name: CARMELINA

units.text: I told Lorenzo in March. I told you both in April. You pretended you'd misheard.
units.name: ISOTTA

units.text: I heard.
units.name: ROSALBA

units.text: Mamma, you did not.
units.name: CARMELINA

units.text: I heard. I said to myself: she'll change her mind by June.
units.name: ROSALBA

units.text: It's August.
units.name: ISOTTA

units.text: So I made the dress in August.
units.name: ROSALBA

units.text: You made it for me to wear!
units.name: CARMELINA

units.text: For you to stand in. So I could see how it hangs.
units.name: ROSALBA

units.text: That is the saddest thing I have ever heard.
units.name: ISOTTA

units.text: It's not sad, it's how she is. She sews against reality.
units.name: CARMELINA

units.text: Where do you want me to put the lace?
units.name: ROSALBA

units.text: Carmelina steps off the stool.
The skirt catches on a pin.
A thin tearing sound.
Rosalba holds up the torn hem to the window light.
She does not look at either of them.
